Giving Themselves Away 


It is an axiom of criminal investi- 
gation that most bad criminals cap- 
ture themselves. Especially is this 
the case with murderers. Thomas 
Neill Cream, one of the most cold- 
blooded murderers we have had in 
fifty years, was a remarkable ex- 
ample of this. He was a man who 
had had some sort of medical train-

women to take a pill or a bottle 
of strychnine, Cream could never

wrote them pretending to be a de-

of his, all sorts of people of high

Eventually. the search narrowed it-

its hands, and that treatment is in-

THE SHANGHAI TIMES, WEDNESDAY, AUGUST 7, 1935

Scotland Yard's New Boss
Inherits Vox Populi Critics

LONDON.—When Sir Philip
Game becomes boss of Scotland
Yard next November, he will be
open to fire from many critics.
Such has been the experience
of all his 12 predecessors in the
post, officially styled commis-
sionership of police for the
metropolitan area of London.
The very scope of "The Yard's"
activities makes its chief a hell's
eye for the barbed darts restless
Britisher are fond of throwing
whenever they think their most
venerated liberties are threatened
by a bureaucratic tyrant.
Even a minor change in police
administration may raise a storm
of concern, for the popular mind,
the word bosses are ruthless
autocrats without the regard for
the nation's democratic traditions.
In addition to preserving order
in Greater London's 700 square
miles, the commissioner must be
a born leader of men.
Past bosses have faced bitter
criticism because they allegedly
failed to keep their staffs of
Britain's bobbies as well as men-
tally and physically alert.
Class Prejudices Charged
Much of the public support ad-
ministered to the retiring commis-
sioner, Lord Trenchard, arose
from his efforts to stop what he
called "mental and physical rot"
in the force.
A crop of old men with no
chance of promotion had entered
the force's officer ranks, it was
said. In some cases, in spite
of hiring young college men on
short term appointments not ex-
ceeding 10 years.
A nation-wide cry at once
arose that Trenchard was sociali-
zing the force by introducing
class distinctions. Then the
reverse was the truth was de-
bated hotly by politicians when
the personnel of his special
staff, the new Field Marshal
Lord Byng, is in fact, earned the
respect and admiration of the
Yard's men for keeping the
force with their privileges and
dignity.
It is to carry on this tradition
that the new boss, with two
years of experience in becoming
commissioner, has been chosen to
succeed Trenchard.—A. P.

苏格兰场的新任主管
承继公众舆论的批评

伦敦讯——当菲利普·盖姆爵士（Sir Philip Game）于明年十一月出任苏格兰场主管时，他将面临来自众多批评者的抨击。历任该职的12位前任均有此经历，该职位的正式称谓为“伦敦大都会区警察总监”。“苏格兰场”的职权范围之广，使其主管成为众矢之的，每当不安分的英国人认为其最受尊崇的自由受到官僚暴君威胁时，便乐于向其投掷尖刻的飞镖。即便是警务管理上的微小变动，也可能引发一阵担忧的风暴，因为在大众心目中，“老板”们是无情的专制者，不顾及国家的民主传统。除了维持大伦敦地区700平方英里的秩序外，警察总监还必须是一位天生的领袖。

前任主管们曾面临严厉的批评，原因是他们被指未能使英国的警察队伍在精神和身体上保持警觉。

被指控存在阶级偏见
给予即将离任的总监特伦查德勋爵（Lord Trenchard）的许多公众支持，源于他努力制止他所谓的警队中的“身心腐朽”。据说，一批没有晋升机会的老者进入了警队的警官阶层。在某些情况下，尽管聘用了年轻的大学生，但任期不超过10年。

全国上下立刻响起呼声，指责特伦查德通过引入阶级区分使警队“社会化”。然而，政界人士激烈辩论的事实却恰恰相反：他的特别幕僚人员、新任陆军元帅宾格勋爵（Lord Byng）实际上因维护警队人员的特权和尊严而赢得了苏格兰场警员的尊敬和钦佩。

为了延续这一传统，这位拥有两年代理总监经验的新任主管被选中接替特伦查德。——美联社

Scotland Yard and the methods used by this great institution in combating crime formed the subject of an interesting speech delivered by Mr. B. H. Dennis, Chief of the British Municipal Council Police, at the weekly meeting of the Tientsin Rotary Club recently. Mr. Dennis remarked in opening that since his arrival in Tientsin quite a number of Britons had approached him and asked what was Scotland Yard. He estimated that at least 80 per cent of the Britons in North China did not know what Scotland Yard really was, so it was hardly surprising that many non-Britishers were in the dark as regards the institution.

Scotland Yard was the Head Quarters of the Metropolitan Police Force in London. There was another force existent in London and they exercised full control over what was reputed to be the richest square mile in the world—the City of London. In this area the City of London Police held sway, and this force had nothing whatever to do with the Metropolitan Police, nor had the Metropolitan Police any power in the City of London. All the rest of London and the Home counties, however, were policed by the Metropolitan Police, and Scotland Yard was responsible for that district. The Metropolitan Police had no power over any of the other police districts in Great Britain. There were occasions, however, when they were invited to assist in solving serious crimes in other districts. It might seem strange that in big cities such as Birmingham and Manchester Scotland Yard had no control, but the fact remained, they only assisted in investigation when invited to do so.

Appointed By Crown

At the head of the Metropolitan Police was the Commissioner of Police of the Metropole, and he was a man appointed by the Crown. It was partly due to this connection with politics that Scotland Yard had so much publicity in the press. Two or three decades ago Scotland Yard was comparatively unheard of, but today one could not pick up a magazine or paper which did not contain some mention of crime and the name of Scotland Yard linked with it. This was due in a large extent to the public's demand for sensation. And so, with publicity from the modern press and through the appointment of the Commissioner, Scotland Yard had become almost a household word. During the past twenty years or so this publicity had been found far from helpful, particularly when it referred to the comings and goings of officers from Scotland Yard in connection with certain crimes.

Appointments of Commissioners had, in recent years, aroused a considerable amount of criticism, Mr. Dennis continued. Prior to the Great War the Commissioner was always a First Classman of great administrative ability and was generally selected from a long and distinguished list of office. During and following the war, however, an entirely different type of man was selected for the post, and the reason for this was that the Government felt that a man well versed in police work was necessary to cope with the new conditions arising out of the war.

Scotland Yard was made up of many departments, the staff being 21,000 in number. It was obvious that with such an organisation there must be other parts than that of detective, yet the public always linked Scotland Yard with detectives, and the papers always referred to "Scotland Yard detectives." Detectives were the real Scotland Yard men, and these were functioning in their own particular branch of crime. They were the experts who dealt with the more serious types of crime, and their work was of a highly specialised nature. 苏格兰场如何运作

前官员向天津扶轮社社员
详细介绍其工作

英国工部局警务处处长 B. H. 丹尼斯（B. H. Dennis）先生最近在天津扶轮社的周会上发表了一次有趣的演讲，主题是苏格兰场以及这一伟大机构在打击犯罪方面所使用的方法。丹尼斯先生在开场时指出，自他抵达天津以来，有不少英国人向他询问什么是苏格兰场。他估计，华北地区至少 80% 的英国人并不知道苏格兰场的真实含义，因此，许多非英国人对这一机构一无所知也就不足为奇了。

苏格兰场是伦敦大都会警察部队（Metropolitan Police Force）的总部。伦敦还有另一支警察部队，他们对据称是世界上最富有的平方英里区域——伦敦市（City of London）——行使完全的控制权。在该区域内，伦敦市警察占据主导地位，这支部队与大都会警察毫无关系，大都会警察在伦敦市也没有任何权力。然而，伦敦的所有其他地区以及本土各郡均由大都会警察负责治安，苏格兰场即对该辖区负责。大都会警察对英国其他任何警察辖区均无管辖权。不过，有时他们会受邀协助其他辖区侦破严重犯罪。在伯明翰和曼彻斯特这样的大城市，苏格兰场没有控制权，这似乎有些奇怪，但事实确实如此，他们仅在受邀时才协助调查。

由王室任命

大都会警察的首长是大都会警察总监，此人由王室任命。部分由于这种与政治的联系，苏格兰场在报纸上获得了大量的宣传报道。二三十年前，苏格兰场还相对默默无闻，但如今，人们拿起任何杂志或报纸，都能看到其中提及犯罪并将苏格兰场之名与之关联的内容。这在很大程度上是由于公众对轰动性新闻的需求。因此，随着现代媒体的宣传以及总监的任命方式，苏格兰场几乎成为了家喻户晓的名称。在过去大约二十年里，人们发现这种宣传远非有益，尤其是当报道涉及苏格兰场警官因某些案件而往来活动时。

THE NORTH-CHINA DAILY NEWS, TUESDAY, NOVEMBER 6, 1934 9526

CRIMINALS AND PASSPORTS

Trade "Non-Existent" in England: Scotland Yard's Way With Traffickers

It appears that the murderer of King Alexander entered France with a forged passport. It is, therefore, reassuring to learn, through a responsible police officer of considerable experience, that the forging of British passports is "practically non-existent."

First, the big international crooks do not use passports—it is much too difficult for them to steal and "doctor" British passports successfully—and, second, international terrorists find it almost impossible to get into Britain, with or without passports.

Why they cannot enter the country is the secret of the Special Branch of Scotland Yard, who exist solely to baulk the political offender, and very wisely they decline to publish the exact details of their methods. The official with whom a representative of "The Observer" spoke remembered in a long experience only two anarchists who succeeded in getting into Britain—"and they were very quickly on their way out again."

There is a difference in this realm between the methods in Britain and those on the Continent, and results point to the British procedure being the more successful. The Continental defence against political crime is more spectacular—that is quite possibly its weakness—than the British which is quieter and more unobtrusive.

Forged Visas

The official who was able to give these reassuring facts stressed that the forging of British passports was almost non-existent, but added that there were cases of the forging of visas. This was a fairly simple matter, requiring only a rubber stamp. The process was known to the police, and whenever movements this way of international crooks or terrorists were reported, this form of forgery was looked for at the ports, and more often than not detected.

It would be as well here to compare the arrangements at the ports in Britain with those on the other side of the Channel; and it was pointed out that, although the passport and immigration officials, the Special Branch, and the C.I.D. were to some extent similar to the corresponding officials on the Continent, close co-operation was a feature of the British system. The method of co-operation is again a matter which the Special Branch prefer to keep to themselves.

It was claimed that murder such as was committed at Marseilles would be impossible in Britain. "When a royal or other distinguished personage is coming to Great Britain," it was stated, "the form of protection to be devised is the duty of the Special Branch of Scotland Yard. Officers who are familiar with the appearances and habits of international crooks, particularly of those with anarchist or Communist tendencies, receive co-operation from the C.I.D. in this way. If the visitor happens to be king of a State in the Balkans, the officers will be fully informed of the districts in London lived in and frequented by people of revolutionary sympathies from that particular country. Facilities will be arranged for the officers to see these people in their haunts, so that they may carry memories of the appearances of the suspects in their minds."

Special Officers

"When the distinguished visitor arrives there will be the usual crowds along the route he is to take, and, incidentally, it would be impossible for him to be left unguarded. Troops, uniformed police officers and plain-clothes detectives line the route in adequate numbers."

Generally, of course, there is little for the uniformed men—troops or police—to do, but valuable work is frequently being done by Special Branch officers all unknown to the thousands of genuine sightseers, whose cheers mark the progress through London of a visiting monarch.

When a foreign monarch came to England some years ago, two Special Branch officers in the crowd that lined the route from the station noticed a face which was familiar to them as one they had seen a good deal in a Soho night cafe. They stationed themselves on either side of him, with their elbows almost meeting in front of the man's stomach. He was a disgruntled native of the visiting king's country. He had no weapons on him, however, so that nothing more than close surveillance could be attempted.

On the other hand, had the police officers not fixed him, accomplices standing near, not known to the police by looks possibly, could have handed him revolver or bomb. This man was deported two months later.

To England Without Passport

Curiously enough, the only crooks who seem to use passports are confidence tricksters, and their passports are usually in perfect order. The rest slip into the country in two ways: (1) By means of coastal and tramp steamers, working their passage and slipping ashore when a row has been started and attention diverted or in some similar way, and (2) by using the return halves of excursion tickets from England to the Continent. They do not use passports, forged or otherwise.

As for anarchists and members of terrorist organizations, very few get through to London. First, they realize that there is a distinct lack of fruitful ground for their activities over here, and, second, the way in is too difficult. Hundreds who have never been near London are known by the Special Branch officers in Britain who were quick to go to see the Marseilles film, by the way, to see if they could recognize anybody in the crowd. There may even have been English detectives at Marseilles at the time, for they go abroad to get to know the men who are dangerous, as well as getting information through the International Police Bureau.

The Special Branch work from Scotland Yard, guard prominent British statesmen and politicians, and ensure the safety of visiting monarchs and statesmen. Occasionally they will be attacked in newspapers as a rather useless department: there will be no reply to the attack. Very few people have ever heard of the name of the chief of the Special Branch, and certainly he and his department are not anxious to be in the limelight. Their valuable work is behind the scenes, and their method to know while remaining unknown.

罪犯与护照

英国不存在此类“贸易”：苏格兰场对付贩运者的手段

亚历山大国王遇刺案凶手似乎持伪造护照进入法国。因此，从一位经验丰富且负责的警务官员处获悉，伪造英国护照的行为“几乎不存在”，这令人感到宽慰。

首先，大型国际罪犯不使用护照——因为窃取并“篡改”英国护照对他们来说难度太大；其次，国际恐怖分子无论是否持有护照，都几乎不可能进入英国。

他们为何无法入境，这是苏格兰场特别处（Special Branch）的秘密，该部门存在的唯一目的便是挫败政治犯，而他们非常明智地拒绝公布其方法的具体细节。接受《观察家报》代表采访的这位官员在漫长的职业生涯中，只记得有两名无政府主义者成功进入英国——“但他们很快就被驱逐出境了。”

在这一领域，英国的方法与欧洲大陆的方法存在差异，而结果表明英国的程序更为成功。欧洲大陆针对政治犯罪的防御措施更为引人注目——这很可能正是其弱点所在——相比之下，英国的手段则更为低调和不显眼。

伪造签证

能够提供这些令人安心事实的官员强调，伪造英国护照的情况几乎不存在，但他补充说，确实存在伪造签证的案例。这是一件相当简单的事情，只需要一枚橡皮图章即可。警方知晓这一手法，每当有关于国际罪犯或恐怖分子以此方式流动的报告时，港口方面就会重点排查此类伪造行为，并且大多能被发现。

在此不妨将英国港口的安排与英吉利海峡对岸的安排进行比较；有人指出，尽管护照和移民官员、特别处以及刑事调查局（C.I.D.）在某种程度上与欧洲大陆的相应官员类似，但密切合作是英国体系的一个特点。至于合作的具体方式，同样是特别处倾向于保密的事项。

据称，像在马赛发生的那类谋杀案在英国是不可能发生的。“当王室成员或其他显贵人物即将来到大不列颠时，”据悉，“制定保护方案是苏格兰场特别处的职责。熟悉国际罪犯外貌和习惯的警官，特别是那些具有无政府主义或共产主义倾向的罪犯，会以这种方式得到刑事调查局的配合。如果来访者是巴尔干某国的国王，警官们将充分了解伦敦内来自该特定国家、具有革命同情心的人士居住和经常出没的区域。当局会安排警官前往这些人的聚集地进行观察，以便他们将嫌疑人的外貌特征牢记于心。”

特别警官

“当显贵访客抵达时，其预定路线上通常会有人群聚集，而且顺便说一句，他绝不可能处于无人 guard 的状态。军队、身着制服的警察和便衣侦探会以充足的兵力沿路线部署。”

当然，一般来说，身着制服的人员——无论是军队还是警察——很少有事可做，但特别处警官却在成千上万 genuine 观光客不知情的情况下频繁开展有价值的工作，这些观光客的欢呼声标志着来访君主在伦敦的行进过程。

几年前，当一位外国君主访问英国时，两名特别处警官在车站沿线的人群中注意到一张面孔，他们很熟悉这张脸，因为在苏荷区（Soho）的一家夜间咖啡馆里曾多次见过此人。他们分别站在此人两侧，手肘几乎在此人腹部前方相接。此人是来访国王所在国家的一名心怀不满的本国人。然而，他身上没有携带武器，因此除了严密监视外，无法采取其他行动。

另一方面，如果警察没有盯住他，站在附近、警方可能并不认识其相貌的同伙本可以将左轮手枪或炸弹递给他。此人于两个月后被驱逐出境。

无护照进入英国

奇怪的是，似乎只有诈骗犯才使用护照，而且他们的护照通常手续完备。其余的人则通过两种方式溜进该国：(1) 搭乘沿海轮船和不定航线货轮，通过打工抵船费，并在发生争执转移注意力或以其他类似方式时溜上岸；(2) 使用从英国到欧洲大陆的 excursion 票的回程联。他们不使用护照，无论是伪造的还是其他的。

至于无政府主义者和恐怖组织成员，极少有人能潜入伦敦。首先，他们意识到这里缺乏有利于其活动的肥沃土壤；其次，入境途径过于困难。数百名从未靠近过伦敦的人都被英国的特别处警官所熟知；顺便提一句，这些警官急于去观看关于马赛的影片，看看能否在人群中认出任何人。当时甚至可能有英国侦探身在马赛，因为他们出国不仅是为了通过国际警察总局获取情报，也是为了结识那些危险人物。

特别处从苏格兰场开展工作，保卫英国重要的政治家和政客，并确保来访君主和政治家的安全。偶尔，他们会遭到报纸攻击，被指责为一个相当无用的部门：对此攻击不予回应。极少有人听说过特别处处长的名字，显然他和他的部门也不渴望成为公众关注的焦点。他们有价值的工作是在幕后进行的，他们的方法是“在保持匿名的同时了解一切”。

Scotland Yard and its Criminals
(Continued from page 5)

reason for requiring help. Suppose some householder complained to the police that a woman had called at his place of residence and produced a letter from a clergyman, telling her that if she came to Salford she could be reunited with the child she had not seen for two years. The M.O. system would enable the investigating officer to turn up all the women in London who have ever been convicted of that trick before and, fortified with a description of the woman, the detective will have little difficulty, if she is still in London, in running her down.

Giving Themselves Away
It is an axiom of criminal investigation that most bad criminals capture themselves. Especially is this the case with murderers. Thomas Neill Cream, one of the most cold-blooded murderers we have had in fifty years, was a remarkable example of this. He was a man who had had some sort of medical training; and his practice was to induce women to take a pill or a bottle of strychnine. Cream could never resist writing letters. Sometimes he wrote them pretending to be a detective; sometimes he wrote accusing perfectly innocent people of the murder. In fact, this was a mania of his, all sorts of people of high and low degree coming under the accusation. The man's vanity was such that even at the inquest on his victims he wrote to the coroner indignant letters, telling him where the medical evidence was wrong. But, as I say, his chief mania was accusing people who had nothing whatever to do with the crimes. Eventually the search narrowed itself down to Neill Cream, and finally he was arrested, convicted and hanged. There is no doubt whatever that he was a systematic poisoner, both in England and America. He had been found guilty in the second degree of the murder of a woman in Chicago, and had served ten years.
Seddon was a murderer who would have escaped all consequence of his act if he had not been so mean that he refused to give even a small portion of the money which his victim had left to one of her relations. Crippen would have escaped detection if he had not run away and emphasised his own guilt. Armstrong would have escaped punishment if, after a successful murder, he had not attempted another, which drew attention to the curious circumstances of his wife's death. Although he had been privately warned that the police were investigating the matter, and that he would be arrested on the morrow, when he was taken into custody they found in his pocket a small package of arsenic. A murderer who had buried the body of his victim in the centre of a chicken run, after watching the fruitless efforts of detectives to discover the body by digging all round his farm, jokingly suggested that they should dig in the run, which they did, and found the terrible evidence they sought. But with all the assistance which murderers give to their captors, it requires a keen analytical brain to utilise the opening which a criminal has offered.

An Aid to Truthfulness
Some day it will be recognised that the protection of the people is of infinitely greater importance than the private rights of citizens, and the method which has been tried with success in America will be universally adopted. This is known as "the scopolamin method." The man to be questioned is given an injection of scopolamin, which is a drug used to induce what is commonly known as twilight sleep. He is placed in a dark room and questioned. Under the influence of this drug the brain is incapable of inventing, and questions asked are invariably answered truthfully. So far it has not been employed to bring criminals to justice, but it has established the innocence of more prisoners than one serving long terms for offences of which they were not guilty. American justice demands, however, that no man should be convicted on any statement that he makes under such an influence, and judges are chary of countenancing this system. Nevertheless, it is infallible, and some day a realist will come along who will consider that it is much more important that the truth should be known and the guilty punished than that a misguided sense of fair play which can only favour the guilty should be satisfied. In the meantime Scotland Yard pursues its breezy and intelligent way without the aid of dope or bludgeon.
Between Scotland Yard and its criminals there is a peculiar relationship which it is difficult to define, and which I think I have illustrated best in the Sooper stories I have told. There is a great deal of good-natured badinage between them. On the one side a spurious, even humble respect; on the other an invincible scepticism. The respect is mixed with a considerable amount of private vituperation. Most habitual criminals know that the detective officer will go far out of his way to do them some legitimate turn. They know he will say what there is to be said in their favour, and that he is the means of communicating with their friends and relations, providing the message is a legitimate one. The criminal knows, too, that when a detective officer says he will notify relations and attempt to obtain bail, he will keep his word, and there is no real resentment at his anti-criminal activities. The number of known criminals who violently resist arrest is very small. To 'go quietly' is the unwritten law of their world. It is only the amateur who has to be carried to the station.
It is true to say that every man who is known to get his living consistently by dishonest means is known personally to the police, and with the assistance of the criminal index it is possible to get immediately into touch with the suspect. On the rare occasions when known criminals commit murder their chance of escape is remote. Every year in this country there are between a hundred and two hundred murders. It has never been below a hundred and never above two hundred. It is also a fact which is not generally known, that one murderer out of every four commits suicide. Mr. Arthur Locke, in some interesting statistics on the subject, has called attention to the fact that only one person under the age of sixteen was convicted in ten years until after the War, when there were five convictions during five years, probably due to causes arising out of the War. In this country crime remains at a fairly low level, and the gunman is unknown.

Should Scotland Yard Tell?
The crimes which are on the increase and with which the police find it most difficult to deal, are cases of false pretences. These have increased to a very considerable extent, a fact which the public should recognise, because it is the average householder and the average citizen who are victimised. This is the only type of criminal with which the average man or woman is brought into contact. Beware of the people who call on you with a pathetic story that they need money to get to their home in some distant part of the country owing to some domestic catastrophe which has overtaken them, or to look for work. Usually they pretend to come from some town with which their victim is associated. They take a great deal of trouble to prepare their story so as to make it plausible. Beware, too, of the lady who is selling her jewellery owing to domestic misfortune; also of old soldiers who served in the same regiment as you. I have often wondered why the police do not publish the sub-divisions of their M.O. card in relation to this particular offence, so that the public can be put on their guard against tricks, which though old and well worn enough are quite new to the person who is caught by them.
In conclusion, let me say this about Scotland Yard. In all the world there is no machine quite as efficient or as free from outside influences. Lord's son and cook's son get exactly the same treatment at its hands, and that treatment is invariably fair.

苏格兰场与其罪犯
（续第5页）

需要求助的原因。假设某户主向警方投诉，称一名女子来到其住所，出示了一封牧师的信，信中告诉她，如果她前往索尔福德（Salford），就能与两年未见的孩子团聚。“作案手法”（M.O.）系统将使调查警官能够调出伦敦所有曾因此类骗局被定罪的女性记录，并辅以对该女子的体貌描述，如果她仍在伦敦，侦探要将其抓获便易如反掌。

自露马脚
刑事侦查的一条公理是，大多数坏罪犯都是自己把自己送进监狱的。谋杀犯尤其如此。托马斯·尼尔·克里姆（Thomas Neill Cream）是我们五十年来遇到的最冷血的谋杀犯之一，也是这一点的显著例证。他接受过某种程度的医学训练；他的惯用伎俩是诱骗妇女服用药丸或一瓶士的宁（strychnine）。克里姆总是忍不住要写信。有时他伪装成侦探写信；有时他写信诬告完全无辜的人犯有谋杀罪。事实上，这成了他的一种狂躁症，各种地位高低不同的人均遭到他的指控。此人的虚荣心极强，甚至在对受害者进行的死因研讯期间，他还给验尸官写去愤怒的信函，指出医学证据中的错误之处。但是，正如我所说，他主要的狂躁症是诬告与罪行毫无关系的人。最终，搜查范围缩小到尼尔·克里姆身上，最后他被逮捕、定罪并处以绞刑。毫无疑问，他在英国和美国都是一名系统性的投毒者。他曾因在芝加哥谋杀一名妇女而被判二级谋杀罪，并服刑十年。
塞登（Seddon）是一名谋杀犯，如果不是因为他过于吝啬，拒绝将受害者留给其亲属的一小部分钱财交出来，他本可以逃脱其行为的一切后果。克里平（Crippen）如果不是潜逃从而加重了自己的罪责嫌疑，本可以逃避侦测。阿姆斯特朗（Armstrong）如果在成功实施一次谋杀后没有试图再次作案，从而引起人们对其妻子死亡情况的离奇关注，本可以逃脱惩罚。尽管有人私下警告他，警方正在调查此事，且他将于次日被捕，但当他被拘留时，警方在他口袋里发现了一小包砒霜。有一名谋杀犯将受害者的尸体埋在鸡舍中央，在目睹侦探们在他农场周围挖掘却徒劳无功地寻找尸体后，他开玩笑地建议他们应该在鸡舍里挖掘，侦探们照做了，并找到了他们所寻求的可怕证据。但是，尽管谋杀犯为其抓捕者提供了种种协助，仍需具备敏锐的分析头脑才能利用罪犯所提供的突破口。

辅助吐露真言
总有一天，人们会认识到，保护民众比公民的个人权利重要得多，而在美国已成功试行的方法将被普遍采用。这就是所谓的“东莨菪碱法”（scopolamin method）。受审问者会被注射东莨菪碱，这是一种用于诱导俗称“朦胧睡眠”（twilight sleep）状态的药物。他被置于暗室中接受讯问。在这种药物的影响下，大脑无法编造谎言，所提问题 invariably（总是）得到如实回答。迄今为止，该方法尚未用于将罪犯绳之以法，但它已证明多名因未犯之罪而服长期徒刑的囚犯是无辜的。然而，美国的司法制度要求，不得仅凭某人在此种影响下所作的陈述对其定罪，法官们对认可这一体系持谨慎态度。尽管如此，它是万无一失的，总有一天会出现一位现实主义者，他认为查明真相并惩罚有罪者，远比满足一种只会偏袒有罪者的、被误导的公平感更为重要。与此同时，苏格兰场在不借助毒品或棍棒的情况下，继续以其轻松而明智的方式行事。
在苏格兰场与其罪犯之间存在着一种难以定义的奇特关系，我认为我在讲述的苏珀（Sooper）故事中对此作了最好的阐释。双方之间存在着大量善意的戏谑。一方面是一种虚假的、甚至是谦卑的尊重；另一方面则是不可战胜的怀疑态度。这种尊重夹杂着相当多的私下辱骂。大多数惯犯都知道，侦探警官会不辞辛劳地为他们做一些合乎规矩的好事。他们知道他会说对他们有利的话，并且只要信息内容正当，他就是与他们亲友联络的渠道。罪犯也知道，当侦探警官表示将通知其亲属并尝试获取保释时，他会信守承诺，因此对他的反犯罪活动并没有真正的怨恨。激烈抗拒逮捕的已知罪犯人数极少。“乖乖就范”是他们那个世界里不成文的法律。只有业余罪犯才需要被押送到警局。
可以说，每一个已知靠不诚实手段持续谋生的人，都为警方所 personally（个人）熟知，并且在犯罪索引卡的协助下，可以立即与嫌疑人取得联系。在已知罪犯犯下谋杀罪的罕见情况下，他们逃脱的机会微乎其微。在这个国家，每年发生的谋杀案在一百至二百起之间。从未低于一百起，也从未高于二百起。还有一个不为大众所知的事实，即每四名谋杀犯中就有一人自杀。阿瑟·洛克（Arthur Locke）先生在一些关于该主题的有趣统计数据中，提请人们注意这样一个事实：在战前十年间，只有一名十六岁以下的人被定罪；而在战后五年间，则有五起定罪，这可能是由战争引发的原因所致。在这个国家，犯罪率保持在相当低的水平，持枪歹徒则闻所未闻。

苏格兰场是否应该公开？
呈上升趋势且警方觉得最难处理的犯罪是虚假借口类案件。这类案件已大幅增加，公众应当认识到这一事实，因为受害的往往是普通户主和普通公民。这是普通男女唯一会接触到的罪犯类型。要提防那些带着悲惨故事上门的人，他们声称由于遭遇家庭变故，需要钱返回国内遥远地区的家乡，或者需要钱去找工作。通常他们假装来自与受害者有关联的某个城镇。他们费尽心机编造故事，使其听起来合情合理。还要提防因家庭不幸而出售珠宝的女士；以及曾在与你相同的团服役的老兵。我常常纳闷，警方为何不公布针对此类特定罪行的“作案手法”卡片细分内容，以便让公众警惕这些骗局，这些骗局虽然陈旧且被反复使用，但对于中招的人来说却是全新的。
最后，让我谈谈苏格兰场。在全世界，没有任何机构像它这样高效且不受外部影响。勋爵的儿子和厨师的儿子在这里受到完全相同的对待，而且这种对待 invariably（总是）是公平的。
